governance_branch_layout.description: Governs the Radicle repository layout: main (released data/, written only by the release script), develop (accepted proposals, written by the tally script), proposals/<entry_id>-<unix_ts> (one new version object per branch), forks/<fork_name> (a group's own data/ tree) and ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName> (live session artefacts, written by pushers). Tunable: release.cadence_s (604800 = 7 days) between data-vX.Y.Z tags; clients compare rules_snapshot_commit at session open. file_rules: never edit a version in place, ids are never reused, proposals touch one entry unless produced by the rebalance script. The runtime deviates: peer.mjs writes only ActiveDimensions/<dim> (dimension.json + doors/<peer>.json) into each peer's own Radicle namespace and mirrors it via git-remote-rad; no release script, tally script, main / develop merge or proposals/* branch exists in code — tools/rebalance.mjs --apply appends proposal versions straight into data/. Context assumed: branch (name string), writer.role (release_script | tally_script | proposer | rebalance_script | fork_owner | pusher), now_s, last_release_s, entry_id, unix_ts, fork_name, dimension.name.

prerequisites.description: The branch matches one of the five layout patterns.
branches.main.writes: only the release script merges develop into main.
branches.develop.writes: only the tally script merges proposals/* into develop.
branches.proposals.writes: the proposer, the rebalance script (counter-proposals) and vote_log appends.
branches.ActiveDimensions.writes: elected pushers only (peer.mjs: every peer, in its own namespace).

proposals/<entry_id>-<unix_ts>.
forks/<fork_name>.
ActiveDimensions/<DimensionName> (what peer.mjs actually pushes).

validation.description: The five branch patterns stay exactly as canonical.
Each branch entry documents content and writes.

At least the three file rules remain and the never-edit-in-place rule is among them.

governance_voting.description: Governs how proposal versions gain weight and change status. Tunables: tally_interval_s (3600) between tallies; quorum_voters (7) distinct voters; accept_threshold (0.6) and reject_threshold (-0.3) on the tally weight; min_age_s (86400) before acceptance; max_age_s (2592000) after which an under-quorum proposal is rejected; per_collection_overrides raise accept_threshold / quorum for concept, stats, elements (0.9 / 25), rules and sync_protocol (0.75 / 15) and governance (0.8 / 20). Vote weight w = 0.01 x (1 + log2(1 + times_used_in_dimension)) x (1 + 0.1 x dimensions_played_in) capped at 0.10 — json-logic has no log2, so the runtime supplies log2_1p_times_used. Tally weight = clamp(sum(+1 w) - sum(-1 w), 0, 1); canonical when weight >= accept AND voters >= quorum AND age >= min_age AND rebalance within tolerance; rejected when weight <= reject OR age > max_age without quorum; the previous canonical becomes superseded at new weight - 0.01. The runtime deviates: no tally runs anywhere; tools/rebalance.mjs --apply appends proposals at weight 0 and status proposal, and peer.mjs pickActive loads the highest-weight version that is neither rejected nor superseded (the engine's activeVersion only excludes rejected). Context assumed: collection, proposal_meta {age_s, voters}, votes {plus: [w], minus: [w]}, scores {current, proposal}, log2_1p_times_used, dimensions_played_in, voter.pubkey, vote_key, votes_seen_keys, now_s, last_tally_s.

Tally weight >= the collection's accept_threshold (override or base).

who_may_vote: any peer with a signing key.
vote_integrity: one vote per (peer_id, entry_id, version).

effects.description: 0.01 x (1 + log2(1 + times_used)) x (1 + 0.1 x dimensions_played_in), log2 supplied as log2_1p_times_used.
The per-peer weight capped at 0.10.
clamp(sum(+1 w) - sum(-1 w), 0, 1).
per_collection_overrides.<collection>.accept_threshold or the base accept_threshold.
per_collection_overrides.<collection>.quorum_voters or the base quorum_voters.
proposal_lifecycle at tally time: canonical | rejected | proposal.
The previous canonical keeps new weight - 0.01 as the fallback.
A tally runs every tally_interval_s.
Minimum tallies a proposal waits through: min_age_s / tally_interval_s (24).

validation.description: 0 < accept_threshold <= 1.
reject_threshold < 0 and not below -1.
quorum_voters is an integer >= 1.
0 < tally_interval_s <= min_age_s < max_age_s.

Every override keeps accept_threshold in (0,1] and at least the base, and quorum at least the base quorum.

governance_rebalance_script.description: Governs the deterministic rebalance pass every proposal goes through. power_score per collection (effect, skill, class, creature, character) is the JsonLogic of logic_rules power_score_*; tolerance.per_entry_relative (0.15): a proposal passes as-is when |score(proposal) - score(current)| <= 0.15 x current; tolerance.per_collection_mean_drift (0.05): otherwise the counter-deltas must bring the rebalance_links closure mean back within 5 %. counter_proposal_algorithm: delta = proposal - current; walk rebalance_links breadth-first (depth <= 2) distributing -delta proportionally to each linked entry's score; a nerf first tries a compensating property on the same entry; counters land on the same proposals/* branch; run every tally_interval_s and on every push. The runtime: tools/rebalance.mjs implements steps 1-5 (validate, score, 15 % test, BFS counters, report to tools/out/) and with --apply appends versions at weight 0 directly into data/ — there is no proposals/* branch, and the mean-drift check (per_collection_mean_drift) is not applied. Context assumed: collection, data (the version's data for scoring), scores {current, proposal, closure_mean_current, closure_mean_proposal}, link.score, links.scores, now_s, last_run_s.

prerequisites.description: Both power scores are numbers.
A power_score formula exists for the collection (effects, skills, classes, creatures, characters); other collections skip the rebalance.
Accept as-is: |delta| <= per_entry_relative x current.
Or the linked counter-deltas keep the closure mean within per_collection_mean_drift.
run_at: every tally_interval_s (or immediately on a new proposal push).

effects.description: power_score(proposal) - power_score(current canonical).
|delta| <= per_entry_relative x current.
delta < 0: prefer a compensating property on the same entry.
The absolute band a proposal may move inside: per_entry_relative x |current|.
-delta x link.score / sum(links.scores): the share of the compensation one linked entry absorbs.
power_score of {data} by collection — the same formulas tools/rebalance.mjs evaluates.

validation.description: 0 < per_entry_relative <= 0.5.
0 < per_collection_mean_drift <= per_entry_relative.
power_score keeps exactly effect, skill, class, creature, character.
counter_proposal_algorithm keeps at least the delta / accept / distribute steps and names rebalance_links.

governance_forks.description: Governs forks: forks/<name> starts as a copy of develop; Dimensions opened under a fork record the fork's rules_snapshot_commit and only players on that fork can join; fork owners vote with the same rules inside the fork; merging back opens proposals/fork-<name>-<ts> with the full diff, judged as one proposal with the accept_threshold of the strictest touched collection and quorum doubled; the rebalance script may split it per entry when split_allowed is set. The runtime: no fork tooling exists — peer.mjs plays one data/ tree and writes rules_snapshot_commit 'local'; nothing checks a joiner's snapshot against the Dimension's. Context assumed: branch, touched_collections (ids), fork_name, unix_ts, dimension.rules_snapshot_commit, me.rules_snapshot_commit, branch.split_allowed.

prerequisites.description: A fork lives at forks/<name>.

merge_back: the proposal branch is proposals/fork-<name>-<ts>.
A merge-back diff touches at least one collection.

proposals/fork-<name>-<ts>.
partial_merge: the rebalance script may split the fork proposal per entry when split_allowed is set on the branch.

validation.description: create, play, merge_back and partial_merge stay the four sections.
Every section is a documented string.
merge_back still applies the strictest threshold and a doubled quorum.

governance_write_permissions.description: Governs which governance route may write each collection: vote-driven (rules, battle_system, actions, effects, skills, classes, characters, creatures, terrain_items, game_modes, sync_protocol, hashgraph_events, dimension_session, governance) go through proposals/* + governance_voting; paper-only (stats, elements) need the concept-level thresholds (0.9 / 25 voters); rebalance-only (concept) text may change only alongside a rebalance report; resolution-vote (contradictions) picks a winning resolution that becomes a new version on the source entries. Every known collection except logic_rules is covered exactly once. The runtime: no write check exists — tools/rebalance.mjs --apply writes any collection's data/ file; peer.mjs only reads data/. Context assumed: collection, branch, policy (route name), votes.weight, proposal_meta.voters, rebalance_report.

prerequisites.description: The collection is listed under the route being used.
vote-driven collections are written through a proposals/* branch.
paper-only collections need governance_voting's concept override (weight >= 0.9, voters >= 25).
rebalance-only collections change only alongside a rebalance report.
resolution-vote collections need the winning resolution id.
